study type: Secondary analysis of cross-sectional survey data
exposure: COVID-19 pandemic period (pre-pandemic, COVID-19 onset, COVID-19 era/recovery)
outcome: Maternal healthcare utilization (adequate antenatal care, home births, C-sections)
cohort: The cohort consists of births recorded in the 2022 Kenya Demographic and Health Survey, analyzed across pre-pandemic, COVID-19 onset, and COVID-19 era/recovery periods.
finding: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted both routine and lifesaving maternal healthcare in Kenya, leading to a lower likelihood of adequate antenatal care and disproportionate effects on certain population subgroups.
mod_finding: Births during COVID-19 onset showed a 31% lower likelihood of occurring via C-section compared to the pre-pandemic period.
cross-section timing: Data from the 2022 Kenya Demographic and Health Survey covered births occurring before March 2020, during March-December 2020, and from 2021-2022.
